title: A Couple Planning the Week's Meals
script: Nadia: [practical] Before we go shopping, let's actually plan the week. We keep buying random things and wasting food.
Bima: [agreeing] You're right, half the fridge went bad last week. What should we cook on Monday?
Nadia: Something quick, since we both work late. Maybe fried rice with whatever vegetables we already have.
Bima: Good idea, that uses up the leftover carrots too. What about Tuesday?
Nadia: Chicken soup. It's easy, and we can make enough for two days if we cook a bigger pot.
Bima: I like that. Less cooking on Wednesday sounds great after a long day.
Nadia: [excited] For Wednesday, let's do something new. There's that noodle recipe you saved a few weeks ago.
Bima: Oh, the spicy noodles? Yes, let's finally try that. We keep saying we will and never do.
Nadia: Exactly, this week we actually commit. Thursday, maybe something simple again, like grilled fish.
Bima: Fish is good. We haven't had it in a while, and it's fast to cook after work.
Nadia: [relieved] Friday, let's just order something. We deserve a break by the end of the week.
Bima: Agreed, no cooking on Friday, that's basically a rule now.
Nadia: Okay, so for the shopping list, we need rice, vegetables, chicken, noodles, and fish.
Bima: Don't forget the spices for the noodles. We're missing at least two of them.
Nadia: [thoughtful] Right, adding those now. Should we also buy fruit for snacks, so we stop buying chips constantly?
Bima: Please, yes. I've been eating way too many chips lately, and I know it.
Nadia: Same here, honestly. Fruit is easier when it's already washed and ready in the fridge.
Bima: Let's wash everything as soon as we get home then, so it's actually easy to grab.
Nadia: Good plan. I think this week will feel less chaotic than usual.
Bima: [satisfied] Definitely. Planning ten minutes now saves us from ordering food every single night.
